title: Samosa

seo.title: Authentic Pakistani Samosa Recipe: Easy & Crispy!
seo.metaDescription: Master the art of making authentic Pakistani Samosa with our easy, step-by-step recipe. Get crispy, flavorful Samosas perfect for any occasion!
seo.imageAlt: Authentic Pakistani Samosa recipe served with chutney
seo.imageCaption: Crispy, golden-brown Pakistani Samosas, a perfect appetizer for any gathering.

description: Samosas are a beloved Pakistani snack, featuring a crispy, golden-brown pastry filled with a savory mixture of spiced potatoes and peas. These triangular delights are a staple for tea-time, Iftar during Ramadan, or any festive gathering. Their irresistible crunch and aromatic filling make them a universally cherished appetizer across the subcontinent.

ingredients.notes: for dough, plus more for frying

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine flour, salt, and carom seeds. Add 4 tablespoons of oil and mix until crumbly. Gradually add water, kneading to form a firm, smooth dough. Cover with a damp cloth and let it rest for 20 minutes.

instructions.title: Cook the Filling Base
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan. Add chopped onion and saute until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Spice the Filling
instructions.text: Add coriander powder, cumin powder, red chili powder, turmeric powder, and salt to the pan. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly to toast the spices. Add green peas and cook for another 3-4 minutes.

instructions.title: Combine Filling Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the mashed potatoes to the pan. Mix well, breaking any large potato chunks with the back of your spoon. Stir in garam masala, dry mango powder, and fresh coriander. Cook for 5 minutes, then let the filling cool completely.

instructions.title: Shape the Samosas
instructions.text: Divide the dough into equal small balls. Roll each ball into an oval shape, about 6-7 inches long. Cut the oval in half. Take one half, moisten the straight edge with water, and form a cone. Fill the cone with 2-3 tablespoons of the potato mixture, then firmly seal the open edges to create a triangular shape.

instructions.title: Heat Oil for Frying
instructions.text: Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or kadai over medium-low heat. Ensure there is enough oil to submerge the samosas partially or fully. The oil should be hot but not smoking, around 300-325°F (150-160°C).

instructions.title: Fry to Golden Perfection
instructions.text: Carefully place the samosas in the hot oil, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Fry the samosas on medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes, turning them occasionally, until they are golden brown and crispy on all sides. This slow frying ensures the crust is fully cooked and flaky.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Remove the fried samosas with a slotted spoon and place them on paper towels to drain excess oil. Serve hot with your favorite mint chutney, tamarind chutney, or ketchup for an authentic Pakistani experience.

tips: For the crispiest samosas, ensure your dough is firm and not too soft. A stiffer dough helps achieve that perfect flaky texture.
Properly sealing the samosa edges with water is crucial to prevent the filling from leaking out during frying. Press firmly to create a strong seam.
Fry samosas on medium-low heat. This allows them to cook through evenly and develop a beautiful golden-brown, crispy exterior without burning.
